rationale: Selected group is the module boundary model.lm_head (torch.nn.modules.linear.Linear, group b57f55423ea79f2933a2, call 777caab7ef6f850ba94458b5, phase microbatch_forward, ranks 0/1, exactly 4 invocations per accumulated step - one per micro-batch, the 4th being the synchronized micro-batch whose backward dispatches the 13 DDP bucket all-reduces). Why the previous boundary must be abandoned rather than repaired again: both prior candidates on the two c10d::allreduce_ functional groups reached the metric floor (63.16-63.61 ms in trial-92d5f02cbf; 60.5-73.2 ms per-rank in trial-d17bd1eb8f's observations) with bitwise-identical gradients, and were rejected solely on step_ms (229.4-258.2 ms vs the 151.86 ms limit, 100% parameter-trial failure). The clean binding-only ablation in the feedback decomposes that failure: parent step_ms 134.787/137.304, passthrough functional binding with candidate computation omitted 228.652/235.029, once-per-step rendezvous 237.479/251.751 - i.e. the legacy functional binding itself, which the framework source (kernel_optimizer/project/binding.py, _create_dispatch_mode/activate) activates as a global TorchDispatchMode around the entire adapter invocation for any bundle containing functional sites (7564 dispatch callbacks + 604 module prehooks per step for 13 target collectives), already violates the constraint before any candidate logic runs. A module-only bundle installs no TorchDispatchMode and no global module hooks: it swaps module.forward for one phase/signature-gated dispatch wrapper costing ~microseconds x 4 calls per step, so the step-time channel that killed both predecessors is removed by construction. Why this group is the right module boundary for the objective: the objective's addressable excess over transport is early-arrival host skew charged into NCCL kernel durations - concentrated in the FIRST collective (execution_timeline-1221e205 seq21: 14.04 ms on rank 0 vs 3.62 ms on rank 1, cross-rank CPU-submit spread 10.4-10.7 ms, both kernels ending within ~90 us; every later kernel at the floor), while the torch_communication-collected baseline (94.49 ms vs rank 1's 63.66 ms and the 62.3/63.4 ms calibration floor from collective_calibration-1af5837f: 3.55-3.66 ms x 12 small buckets + 19.4-19.8 ms large) carries 31-48 ms of skew with direction that flips across collectors (nsys shows rank 1 waiting), so the remedy must be symmetric. model.lm_head is the LAST module executed in the forward pass, immediately before the loss computation and the final backward that fires bucket 0's dispatch - the latest replaceable point upstream of the first allreduce that does not require functional dispatch, minimizing the skew that re-develops between alignment and first dispatch. Bucket 0's parameters (h.11 + ln_f per communication-ownership.json) confirm the first dispatched bucket belongs to the tail of the backward that follows this call site. The replacement calls the unchanged parent via context.references on every invocation, so all 13 allreduce dispatches, the reducer, the NCCL process group, bucket views and bitwise gradient outputs are untouched; the /dev/shm counter page used for the cross-rank arrival rendezvous is named at installation time over the adapter's existing gloo control group, outside every timed or profiled region, exactly as in the prior mechanism-validated trials.
hypothesis: Repair hypothesis for the step_ms rejection, to be tested by actual execution: replace model.lm_head.forward with a wrapper that counts its invocations, publishes a monotonically increasing arrival count to a 16-byte /dev/shm counter page (one int64 per rank, set up once at build() over the existing gloo control group, outside timing), and on every 4th invocation of each 4-micro-batch cycle - the synchronized micro-batch, both ranks counting identical call streams from the frozen workload - performs the symmetric cross-rank arrival rendezvous (tight bounded spin on the peer counter, single budget parameter, graceful degrade: budget expiry proceeds to the parent and repeated timeouts disable the wait while counting continues, so a waiting peer is never orphaned) before calling the unchanged parent op; all other invocations call the parent directly. Expected objective effect: the early rank's host wait replaces the device-side spin inside the first NCCL kernel (which in baseline ends within ~90 us of the peer's kernel regardless of who waits), so the first kernel's duration falls to its ~3.6 ms transport floor and the max-rank kernel-duration median drops from the 94.49 ms baseline toward the 62.3-63.6 ms floor plus a residual for skew re-developing between lm_head and the first dispatch (loss + autograd entry + tail-block backward, ~50-80 host ops: estimated 1-5 ms clean, proportionally more under the torch_communication collector whose per-op recording asymmetry produces the 31-48 ms profiled skew), i.e. an expected ~64-70 ms versus 94.49 ms. Expected step_ms effect (hypothesis, not measurement): the module dispatch adds ~microseconds; the single wait is bounded by the actual cross-rank skew (~10.5 ms in clean runs, the observed CPU-submit spread), occurs while the GPU still holds the final micro-batch's forward tail plus the rank-1-paced NCCL chain as slack, and the prior trials' +9/+17 ms rendezvous cost was measured only on top of the ~95 ms TorchDispatchMode binding that no longer exists here; the clean parent endpoints (134.8/137.3 ms) and the 151.86 ms constraint leave 14-17 ms of measured headroom against a wait of at most the skew, with the budget/degrade path bounding the worst case at baseline behavior. Quality expectations: every invocation still executes the parent op with unmodified arguments (4 reference calls per step, full coverage of the single selected call), gradients remain bitwise identical across ranks as measured twice on this exact rendezvous mechanism (max_abs_error 0.0 over 248,879,621 compared elements in trial-92d5f02cbf), and no gloo collective, NCCL kernel or CUDA work is added inside any timed or profiled region.
